blocks.text: # Competitive Landscape — Proofpress

Scan date: 2026-07-18 (all numbers verified live via GitHub API / web this date; no ⚠️ items outstanding).
Framework: our position is the intersection of four adjacent categories; **one direct neighbor now exists (Kortix, see Threat ranking)**.

Our claim to defend: knowledge-work orchestration + versioned artifacts with review loop (draft → assign → request changes → warm-session revision → approve) + multi-harness + self-hosted multiplayer.
## Bucket 1 — General agent workspaces ("single-player open Cowork")
Have: agents doing knowledge work, self-hosting. Lack: versioning, review, multi-agent supervision.

| Project | Stars | License | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| zhayujie/CowAgent | 46.0k ✅ | MIT | README deep-read 2026-07-18: personal assistant, single-agent-per-instance, IM-channel-first (WeChat/Feishu/DingTalk/Telegram…), Markdown-wiki memory but **no versioning, no review loop, no multiplayer**. Threat rating **confirmed: low direct / mindshare only** — Chinese community momentum is the asset; the architecture points away from team orchestration. |
| lobehub/lobehub | 80.5k ✅ | fair-code (NOASSERTION) | Launched "Chief Agent Operator" 2026-05-18 (Product Hunt #1 of day): hires agents from 273k-skill marketplace, runs Claude Code/Codex/OpenClaw 24/7 in cloud, **reports via daily brief** in Slack/Discord/WeChat etc. Reporting ≠ review — no versioned artifact, no approval gate — but hiring/scheduling/reporting vocabulary is one step from assignment/review. Highest-trajectory threat in bucket. |
| kortix-ai/suna → **Kortix** | 20.0k ✅ | source-available (was Apache-2.0) | **Moved buckets — see Threat ranking.** Pivoted to "The Company AI Command Center". Source deep-read 2026-07-18 (change-requests.ts, review-items.ts, git/merge.ts): Review Center is a real inbox product (output/decision/batch kinds + CR/approval adapters, 5 verdicts, risk levels, Slack/Teams cards) and **request-changes auto-flows back to the originating session's agent, waking sleeping sandboxes** — they have a warm-revision loop. But CR core is "intentionally minimal" (their comment): git-branch metadata, no review/comment tables, feedback = flat text log in jsonb, **diff = unified git patch only, explicitly no semantic diff for markdown/docx**; versioned unit is the repo/branch, never the artifact. Pre-1.0 (v0.9.98). |
| FoundationAgents/OpenManus | 57.5k ✅ | MIT | **Dormant — last push 2026-02-11.** Downgraded to non-threat; star count is a fossil. |
| OpenHands/OpenHands | 81.2k ✅ | NOASSERTION (relicensed from MIT) | Moved to own org. Coding-centric, strong eval culture; still git-native. |
| microsoft/magentic-ui | 10.0k ✅ | MIT | Now "MagenticLite" (browser + local FS agent). Still best-in-class human-in-the-loop approval UX to study; different domain. |
| skalesapp/skales | 1.2k ✅ | NOASSERTION | Personal AI desktop agent. Watch consumer polish only. |

Assessment: the bucket's leaders are converging on our metaphors faster than expected — lobehub shipped "hiring/reporting", Kortix graduated out of the bucket entirely by shipping review. The 6–12 month window estimated last scan was wrong: **it was ~0 months for Kortix**. What remains open: non-git artifacts, harness neutrality, true open-source license.
## Bucket 2 — Coding orchestration (our shape, wrong domain)
Have: boards, parallel sessions, review loops. Lack: anything non-git.

| Project | Stars | License | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator (AO) | 8.3k ✅ | Apache-2.0 | Desktop agent-IDE, 23 harness adapters, worktree isolation, CI/review/merge loops. Reference for supervision UX; git-native to the bone. |
| omnigent (our base) | active ✅ | Apache-2.0 | Session abstraction is domain-neutral — our structural advantage. |
| farion1231/cc-switch | 118k ✅ | MIT | Harness cockpit/router, not orchestration; owns "many harnesses, one surface" mindshare. |
| ruvnet/ruflo | 65.0k ✅ | MIT | README deep-read 2026-07-18: swarm coordination + vector memory + federation built around **Claude Code specifically** — despite "meta-harness" branding it is monolithic to its own harness. No versioned-artifact model; review exists only as sparse "before-merge gates" checklist items. More engineering-real than expected (benchmarks, ADRs, honest status page) but aimed at agent autonomy, not human review of deliverables. Threat rating **confirmed: low-moderate** — dangerous only if federation + team workflows (both in active dev) pivot toward artifact review. Re-check quarterly. |
| BloopAI/vibe-kanban | 27.4k ✅ | Apache-2.0 | Board-of-agents validated; last push 2026-04-24 — momentum cooling. |
| claude-squad, Conductor, Terragon | small/closed | — | Same category, same ceiling. |

Assessment: commoditizing; still nobody positioned for knowledge work — their data model IS git. Validates our "session-native, not git-native" bet. Note Kortix chose the git data model for its company product — that's the bet we're on the other side of.
## Bucket 3 — Open-source system-of-record with AI bolt-ons
Have: docs/tasks/teams as durable record. Lack: agent-native execution (with one exception now).

| Project | Stars | License | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| AppFlowy | 74.0k ✅ | AGPL-3.0 | Notion alt + AI workspace. |
| AFFiNE | 70.6k ✅ | MIT + ee (NOASSERTION) | Doc/whiteboard + AI copilot. |
| **Plane** | 54.7k ✅ | AGPL-3.0 | **Moved. Already shipped** (plane.so/ai): agents as assignees ("add an agent as an assignee just like any teammate"), native MCP server, @mention agent framework, Agent Run lifecycle tracking, audit trail, and configurable **"what needs human review"** gates. The predicted "natural move" happened. Review is of task execution, not versioned artifacts — but they own record + workflow + now rent execution. |
| Huly (hcengineering/platform) | 26.9k ✅ | EPL-2.0 | All-in-one PM; team-of-agents marketing. |
| Outline | 39.7k ✅ | BSL (NOASSERTION) | Team wiki + AI answers. |

Assessment: the structural blocker (continuous human editing vs propose-review-merge) still holds for docs — but Plane shows the task side of the record can absorb agents fast. Partnership-target logic still applies to the doc-first players; Plane graduates to watched competitor.
## Bucket 4 — The review/version layer for agent output
Our core IP. Nearest neighbors:

- docs-as-code (Git+Markdown review flows): right mechanics, failed adoption — humans won't pay the ceremony. Our why-now: agents absorb it.
- Workflow builders (Dify 149.2k ✅, n8n, Flowise): human-approval nodes are a gate in a DAG, not review of a versioned artifact with warm-session feedback. Biggest enterprise-sales competitor, not product competitor.
- eval/guardrail tooling (LangSmith et al.): reviews runs, not deliverables.
- Direct implementations of semantic-diff + warm-session review over non-git artifacts: **still none found ✅** — Kortix is the closest but rides git commits/PRs.
## Threat ranking (revised 2026-07-18)

1. **Anthropic ships multiplayer/versioned Cowork** — highest impact. Structural counter unchanged: open + any-agent + self-hosted. Never trade those.
2. **Kortix (ex-Suna)** — ⬆ from "would become a competitor" to **shipped the closest thing to our loop**, including automatic feedback-to-agent revision (verified in source 2026-07-18). What they have NOT built — and are structurally biased against, since git is their declared source of truth — is exactly our core: artifact-level identity/history, semantic diff, content-anchored review comments. Our remaining edges: (a) artifact-native data model + semantic diff vs their branch-metadata + line patches, (b) they went source-available while we stay genuinely open, (c) multi-harness neutrality vs their own runtime, (d) pre-1.0 immaturity. Watch monthly; this is the sharpest external clock on M0/M1.
3. **lobehub adds review loop** — high likelihood; CAO launch shows velocity and the vocabulary is adjacent. Counter: ship fast, own the vocabulary publicly first (see Tactics).
4. **Plane** — ⬆ from mid-term to **already executing**: agents-as-assignees + human-review gates shipped. They'll own record + execution for task-shaped work; counter remains being the artifact/review layer they'd rather integrate than build.
5. **AO expands past git** — low; data model and community are git-native.
6. ~~OpenManus~~ — removed; dormant since Feb 2026.
## Tactics

**Own the vocabulary now.** "Draft → Review → Approve **for agents**" must appear in our launch post, README tagline, and every public description before lobehub or Kortix phrase it first — whoever's words the category adopts defines the category, and this is the cheapest available defense against both. Kortix says "change requests" (developer vocabulary, git frame); lobehub says "hiring/reporting" (HR frame). The Draft/Review/Approve frame (knowledge-work vocabulary, matches our UI terms) is still unclaimed. Deadline: publicly attached to our name before the next scan.
## Standing conclusions

- The four-bucket vacuum has one occupant now (Kortix), but the **non-git, multi-harness, truly-open** cell is still empty — positioning one-liner tightens to: "They version code with git. We version and review what agents produce — docs, decks, analyses — across any agent, on your infra."
- Why-now still holds; the Kortix/Plane moves are confirmation, not refutation — the window is just shorter than last month's estimate.
- Cadence: refresh monthly (four bucket queries + threat check). **Next due: 2026-08-18.** Add Kortix release notes and Plane changelog to the check list.
